paragraphs.source_en: Possible private paintings were often located within the main painted sites such as Sefar or Jabbaren. Next to the large compositions, or more often on neighbouring walls, there are sometimes very small figures which are unlikely to have been produced by a community. It is understandable that if painted sites were considered sacred, everyone visiting them would have wished to add his or her modest personal painting.

paragraphs.source_en: Hunting is not explicit in the Round Head art; however, several images could have been related to this activity, for instance at Uan Mata in the Tassili (Fig. 5-19). This shelter, located on a hill, presents a Round Head figure of a hunter with an arrow in his left hand and probably a bow in his right hand, partly eroded by the ancient waterfall. Since he is facing the underlying plain, one can imagine a real hunter standing in this shelter and observing wild animals. The body paintings of the hunter's body and attributes such as horns however rather suggest the spiritual side of hunting.

paragraphs.source_en: There are several representations of what is generally called The Great God (see figure 3-4) (Lhote 1958; Sansoni 1994). These large figures, from around 1. 5 m to 4 m high, are always depicted in the central part of the wall in a dominant position and are apparently all males. With their hands raised and often surrounded by smaller figures they seem to represent an important figure in the spiritual life. All Great Gods are painted in the same style, namely a red border with a white filling, which may indicate that they were created in the same period or that they were important for a certain group who created them. Since they are all situated on the Tassili Plateau they may have belonged only to these most elevated altitudes. Did they represent spirits or gods inhabiting the highest mountains as known from the ethnography?

paragraphs.source_en: At Sefar they are painted inside the stone city and were therefore hidden but at In Eleghi the Great God is located in a shelter exposed to the exterior and visible from a large distance. Their function could therefore have been multiple, involved in rituals in secret places or venerated by a large community when exposed to everyone.

paragraphs.source_en: The ethnographic record testifies that the function of sites and shelters was varied. Considering different morphology and location of shelters with Round Head images we can conclude that hunter-gatherers producing these paintings also used different places for different purposes. The function of some sites or shelters may have been multiple and could also have changed over time.
